sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and imports
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It explains how cost of goods sold is built and loads the helper tools.
sections.why: Gives the reader the formulas before the code.

sections.name: calculate_cogs_line
sections.title: Variable cost for one product line
sections.what: For one product line, grows the cost per unit each year with inflation and multiplies by volume to get that line's variable cost.
sections.why: Each product's cost follows its own volume and inflation, so each line is calculated separately.
sections.watch_out: Results stop at the shorter of the volume list and the cost list, so a mismatch drops years without warning.

sections.name: calculate_fixed_cogs
sections.title: Fixed cost growing with inflation
sections.what: Grows a starting fixed cost by the yearly inflation rates to give the fixed cost for each year.
sections.why: Likely reason: fixed costs are kept apart because they do not follow sales, but they still rise over time.
sections.watch_out: Fixed cost is not linked to sales volume, so higher sales will not raise it.

sections.name: calculate_cogs_full (part 1)
sections.title: Adding up all lines and fixed cost
sections.what: Works out every line's variable cost and the fixed cost, then adds the variable costs of all lines for each year.
sections.why: The model needs one total cost figure for each year.
sections.watch_out: The number of years comes from the longest line, and shorter lines are skipped in the later years without a warning.

sections.name: calculate_cogs_full (part 2)
sections.title: Returning the cost results
sections.what: Packages the line results, fixed cost, variable total, and grand total into one result.
sections.why: Gives the statements builder a single result to read.
sections.watch_out: Total cost adds the two lists by position and stops at the shorter one, so a length mismatch drops years.

summary: Works out the cost of goods sold each year, split into costs that move with volume and costs that stay roughly fixed, with both growing with inflation.
purpose: Produces variable cost per product line, fixed cost, and total cost of goods sold for each year.
why: Cost of goods sold is a major cost in the income statement and drives the stock and supplier-payment balances.
how: 1. For each product line, grow its cost per unit using its inflation rates. 2. Multiply volume by cost per unit and divide by the unit divisor. 3. Add all lines' variable costs for each year. 4. Grow the fixed cost using its inflation rates. 5. Add variable and fixed cost for each year.
inputs: A list of line data (line_id, volumes, base cost per unit, cost inflation rates); a base fixed cost; fixed cost inflation rates; a unit divisor.
outputs: A dictionary with results per line, the fixed cost list, the total variable cost list, and the total cost list.
risks: Years are matched by position, so lists of different lengths are cut short without warning. Fixed cost is not linked to volume, so higher sales do not change it. The unit divisor must match the one used for revenue, or margins will be wrong.
debug: If total cost looks wrong, check each line's volumes and cost per unit first, then the unit divisor. If a line is missing from the totals, check that its line_id matches what the caller expects.
